chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Sa'd ibn Sa'd and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Zakariyya ibn Adam asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), with Safwan present, about what [the ruling is] when the dog and the cheetah kill [prey], so he said, 'Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, "The cheetah and the dog are equal in value."'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Title of Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْفَهْدُ: Cheetah (a type of wild cat used for hunting)
key_terms.صَفْوَانُ: Safwan (A prominent narrator, present during the question)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the equality between a hunting dog and a cheetah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, clarifies that the dog and the cheetah (fahd) are equal in legal valuation (qadr), a principle crucial for determining compensation or ritual purity in hunting contexts. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to distinguishing between domesticated hunting dogs and wild predators, ensuring consistency in fiqh rulings regarding game animals. The hadith underscores the precision of Imami jurisprudence in categorizing animals based on their utility and status in Islamic law.
